Perfume rating 3.79 out of 5 with 3,805 votes

Si Lolita by Lolita Lempicka is a Oriental Floral fragrance for women. Si Lolita was launched in 2009. Si Lolita was created by Christine Nagel and Benoist Lapouza. Top notes are Mandarin Orange and Bergamot; middle notes are Pink Pepper, Elemi resin, Sweet Pea, Heliotrope and Wallflower; base notes are elemi, Patchouli, Tonka Bean and Amber.

Lolita Lempicka presents a new fragrance, Si Lolita, in a gorgeous flacon characteristic for its shamrock shape and fairy-tale design typical for Lolita Lempicka brand. The fragrance was announced as feminine, subtle and ethereal.

Si Lolita is a fragrance of happiness and elixir of love, touch and gentleness, created of oriental-floral rhythms strengthened with spicy accords, bergamot, mandarin, pink pepper, sweet peas, elemi, patchouli, Tonka and amber. The fragrance was created by Christine Nagel and Benoit Lapouza.

Flacon of Si Lolita is shaped like shamrock with four leaves and it is made of glass with golden edges. Each of the leaves is shaped like a heart and it represents woman's beauty, her imagination and emotions… The fragrance is available as 40,50 and 80 ml eau de parfum and we can expect it on the market in August 2009.

_wynona_ 08/10/24 11:16

This was the first perfume I bought as an adult with my own money. I don't remember how I found out about it or why I chose it, but I want to thank 22-year-old me. When I first tried it, I thought it was a bit "advanced" for me, as I was inexperienced and associated perfume with the pretty but slightly "corporate" smells from Burberry or Chanel that my aunt would wear.

Regardless, I fell in love with it. The spicy-sweetness agreed with my skin which instantly eats up the majority of delicate notes from more dainty perfumes. I loved how it almost smelled masculine, like a fresh and spicy cologne a slightly older man would wear. Si Lolita is spunky, fresh in a spicy way like ginger, yet warm in an expansive way. Warm like a fire but not quite cozy like being wrapped up in a cashmere robe. There is movement to this perfume.

This perfume is flirting by the fireplace with a ginger whiskey and sharing a perfect mandarin.
This belongs in my trifecta of favorite spicy fresh perfumes with Lucky Number 6 and ELDO Like This.

fleader 08/04/21 21:07

Si Lolita isn’t a girly scent. It doesn’t contain any notes that read particularly masculine either, but since it is so peppery and dry I could see it working well on anyone, regardless of gender. It does have a youthful and brisk, bracing, even prickly quality to it. I imagine a quick walker and a quick talker wearing this.

It starts off very very peppery, then the elemi comes out, and the the amber and vanilla and heliotrope, and then I can see how it fits in as a Lolita Lempicka scent. The pepper, sweet pea, and patchouli all share a dryness that really keeps the scent feeling weightless and airy. This dryness works beautifully with the elemi which is itself dry and peppery, though it thankfully does NOT smell like a dill pickle here (I have been burned before).

Pamilo 07/05/21 04:24

My batch is an original batch from the 2009 release. On application, there's a momentary 'signature' anise illusion reminiscent of earlier Lempicka creations. It's gone in a moment, but whilst there it's like an aroma of Sambuca or Ricard a table or two distant. There follows spices and resins, topped-off by the pink pepper.

Once the florals pile-in, it's sweet pea and heliotrope (colloquially known as "cherry pie plant" in parts of East Anglia) I notice first. The drier scent of wallflower follows, some varieties of which are described as having a vaguely clove-like fragrance. Amber and tonka serve as a warming foundation on which all else rests. Curiously, patchouli (a favourite of mine that always pings my radar) is the single note I am slow to pick-up on, but does become more discernible deeper into the drydown.

Once it settles, Si Lolita is essentially spicy, balsamic and resinous.

The bottle is a pretty design without being girlie. It is pleasingly eye-catching and reminds me of the classic-chic of Nina Ricci from 40 years ago. Delicate but not fragile.

Si Lolita is one I choose to wear in warmer weather. Womanly and demure.

Our noses mature and tastes change years ago I only enjoyed one type of compositions so when I tried Si Lolita a year after its release I did not like it very much, I never gave it another chance until recently I tried it again and I loved it, that lucky for me to find these two fragrances after so long
I must acknowledge that it is a polarizing and a bit contradictory essence because it is simple and complex at the same time, what characterizes this essence is basically Sweet Pea with a super high dose of pink pepper, this fragrance is quite spicy, with the characteristic sweet touch of pink pepper, when it comes out it feels fresh (bergamot and tangerine) but very spicy due to the aforementioned pink pepper, this initial slap passes quickly and the pepper settles but is present throughout the duration of this fragrance accompanied with a resinous note (elemi resin) and an amber accord and slightly sweet and earthy (amber, tonka bean and patchouli).
This fragrance is further from the concept of the house of enchanted forests and fairy tales and it is presented in a beautiful bottle in the shape of a four-leaf clover with a ball scarf in the purest and most chic Parisian style, the fragrance itself is Inspired by the young years of the designer and if the main objective was to transmit youth and joy, for the year it came out it was a unique fragrance, even today there are very few similar ones and it can be used perfectly by both sexes as it adapts very well to the Today's standards, in addition to having a different shade in each individual, the duration is quite good depending on the factors (although it can be used almost all year round) with a medium projection.

Livvy111 05/09/21 03:29

Bought this without really smelling it before..RISKY but it paid off. I checked reviews at the time and it had 5 stars. So I bought it on offer. One word- Complex in its opening, linear, straightforwards and calming in the drydown. The pepper is quite strong for about 5 minutes and a bit 'fizzy' in the opening. I was a bit worried like 'oh no what have I bought?!' but the dry down is super unusual, and EXPERTLY balanced.

The pink pepper although prominent at first is not sharp and cloying like a lot of modern fragrances. It drys down to a quiet woody floral. I think its great. Very unusual but not offputting. If you smelt this once, you would remember it for a long time. Very distinct.

And the other ingredients do not 'fight for space'. They are complimentary, just sweet and borderline unisex that keeps you wondering what this fragrance wants to be. This fragrance is a bit of a dancer. It moves with time and you cant quite pin it down. I find it really nice to wear. Those who complain of a medicinal dry down- nonsense (for me anyway). Maybe it depends on skin chemistry. I tend to like fragrances with a bit of a mineral/balsamic base note as it keeps me from feeling sick by the end of the day. A little does go a long way. Wonderfully different from all the sickly sweet unoriginal garbage out there.

Enrium 03/23/21 09:23

Having loved Lolita Lempicka, I really wanted to try this one. And I wasn't disappointed! Lolita Lempicka seems to specialise in girly scents, housed in whimsical bottles that are much better than one would expect at face value. Si Lolita is no exception - the quality of the ingredients used and its expert composition make this an impressive addition to an underrated house.

The opening of Si Lolita is a nose-tickling spicy pepper with hints of sweet orange and ginger. The initial spray is like the first sip of a fizzy drink, effervescent and bright, reminiscent of ginger ale with cola-like qualities. It manages not to be too sweet; instead is refreshing and slightly herbal. The patchouli gives it an earthy depth, beautifully complementing the other ingredients from the first spray.

The drydown is more floral, with the powdery resin notes coming to the fore. The spiciness remains, but gently fades as the scent dries down, becoming more musky. A hint of tonka bean is evident as it becomes a skin scent, and the patchouli is the last thing I can smell. Sillage and longevity are moderate.

Another great scent from Christine Nagel, SL is well-blended, fresh and interesting. Spicy citrus done well, with no dreaded potpourri vibes. A decent autumnal feminine fragrance, this is versatile and utterly pleasant throughout. 4/5.

IndiePenScent 02/17/21 15:02

At first spritz I worried that my sample had lost the pepper, because while present, the elemi resin and patchouli were so bold. Then the pepper showed up, probably the pepperiest ladies red pepper I've smelled.

After a few minutes a juicy citrus steps up to swirl it all into a sassy pepper floating in sweet mandarin juice with a good amount of patchouli giving it some depth. As the dry out continues, the flowers further muffle the pepper, and by the end the oily sweetness of the tonka bean, the sweet amber, and the patchouli are all that's left.

I would say the pepper and mandarin stage project the furthest, on me for about twenty minutes in cool weather, and the swirly "stable drydown" stage for a further two hours, maybe three, (and able to be extended with warmth as it resurrected itself every time I had to jump up and run around at work), and the patch/amber/tonka "ghost" stage lasted as a skin scent for several more, only I took a shower before bed and washed it off.

Or in other words: the Wachow! stage lasted from my house clear to my desk at work, the stable drydown hooked compliments from folks until after lunch, and the day finished with a nice quiet skin scent.

The spiciness of Si Lolita is no joke. And this comes from someone who loves big spicy bombs like Kenzo Jungle l'Éléphant and enjoys pink pepper heavy scents like Angel EdT (the comet one) or Twilly Eau Poivrée. Si Lolita is floral, sweet, very feminine ; but it's also sharp, raw, unapologetic, it has a big personality. Pink pepper and elemi smell like essential oils, and there seems to be a good dose of cloves here too. Unfortunately, this reminded me of a personal experience : the smell of my dentist's practice. It was all here : the waiting room, the camphorated and sharp disinfectants, and even the rubbery gloves. The lovely sweet floral notes could not tame the medicinal smell. And I have nothing against medicinal scents in general, but when it comes to something reminding me of the dentist, I really can't. Obviously scent perception and skin chemistry are a very personal thing, and Si Lolita certainly doesn't smell like the dentist to most, or it wouldn't have sold well otherwise. I can easily imagine to some people, this strong spicy accord is quite addictive. Unfortunately, it really doesn't work on me. Not a safe blind buy, but I strongly recommend to anyone who likes pink pepper to get a sample of Si Lolita, as it's truly unique.

I have been coming back to Si, Lolita for years.

Aredore 01/23/16 17:40

I tried Si Lolita years ago when it was part of the regular Sephora lineup. I remembered a curious spicy/sweet perfume that part of me regretted not buying. I got lucky at Marshall's today and found a lone bottle of this unopened and marked down.

Si Lolita is the fresh, bracing sister in the Lolita Lempicka feminine lineup. Built upon the same structure of contrasting dual accords of Floral/Sweet and Resinous/Herbal/Bitter that made the original Lolita so good and so unique even 20 years later, Si swaps out the anisic herbal accord for a double dose of refreshing pink pepper and the moody violets for irrepressible sweet pea. Notes of patchouli and elimi resin - a balsamic note on the lighter, creamier side of Myrrh, Frankincense, and Opoponax, - keep the super sweet florals in-check and the pink pepper party going all the way to the dry down. The final phase is a bitter, dirty amber. Sweet but sharp, Friendly and strong-minded, Si Lolita is a youthful revival of the resinous perfumes of old.

While the bottle and marketing are aggressively girly, this fragrance exposes the fundamental silliness of arbitrarily gendering smells. Guys, girls, and gender non-conformers looking for an unconventional daytime fragrance that won't read on the male/female binary should give this one a test. You might have a new favourite!

lotus and jasmine 03/26/15 14:46

Do you ever get tired of scents that smell the same? Si Lolita doesn't. The notes in the pyramid above say pink pepper, but I do not detect the rosey scent of pink...instead SL opens with a puckishly intense black pepper accord. Charmingly abrasive, refreshing, odd.

SL is confounding at first. Why would anyone want to smell like black pepper? But...you keep sniffing yourself. Over time, the pepper remains, but drifts of sweet pea, heliotrope, and juicy mandarin catch your attention...

Where are they coming from? You sniff your wrist, and it's still crisp, dark pepper. But that sweetness lingers around you, behind you, where ever you least expect it. Si Lolita sneaks up on the wearer. You'll fall in love with her, after you get to know her. Cinnamon, is not listed, but can be found, anise, clove, and fenugreek as well. Surprisingly bright, given the potential darkness of the accords...but that's the point,right?

But on first acquaintance? She's really not what you expect. Particularly not from a brand known for sweet scents. And why would ANYONE create a perfume that smells like black pepper?

Think Audrey Hepburn. Think flying monkeys. Think of the most gloriously unexpected sights you have ever encountered. An elegance comprised entirely of parts that should not harmonize.

Si Lolita is the Pablo Picasso of perfume, the cubist blue, the scent that is too simple to be true. The unexpected, but much anticipated. the Cirque du Soleil of perfume.

Addictive.
Superlative.
Intoxicating.
Invigorating.
Almost too good to be true.

Si Lolita is a lovely uplifting fragrance that's quite unusual, charming and well-blended. I think that this perfume would be the perfect companion for the colder months.

On my skin, this was harsh at first thanks to the citrusy top notes, until lots of skipping pink pepper emerges. This is followed by a dry, resinous and very powdery spicy-floral of which the dry-down is a lighter version. The patchouli gives the composition a bit of earthiness, amber gives warmth, and the tonka bean is what makes this powdery. Sillage is soft to moderate; lasted for about 6-7 hours on me (a few hours more than the EDT).

I have now tested both the EDP and EDT. The EDT is lighter, fresher as it has more floral accords, is less sweet and less peppery. Both are lovely but I do prefer the EDP as I find that it has more pepper and personality :)

Cassiano 05/09/14 09:36

The fragrances of this brand are known for being intense, those that disturb the others, without mercy, always with good projection and longevity.

In 2009, Si Lolita was released in Eau de Parfum concentration, inspired by the Baroque style, in addition to the Parisian culture and nature. The box was inspired by a fabric created by Lolita and the bottle, shaped like a four-leaf clover, was thought to be a jewel, almost a lucky charm, which still brings a handkerchief around the neck, in the purest glamour. It is a floral-oriental, with some spices, composed around the sweet pea flower, which is natural of Sicily and only blooms once a year.

Si Lolita EDP Contains output notes of pink pepper, bergamot, and Mandarin; wallflower (mustard family), sweet pea blossom and Heliotrope, in the heart; elemi, amber, patchouli, and tonka bean, in its base.

The big surprise is that this fragrance is entirely changeable. It can present floral, spicy, medicinal or sweet nuances depending on the skin. When Si Lolita EDP came to the market, pleased a lot for being less "aggressive" than the other fragrances of the brand, winning many female fans. Moreover, became known for its unisex aspect, since some women found that the scent was more masculine than feminine. Most of the women agree with the presence of pepper, which is very strong, going to a floral heart and with a sensual and often medicinal aspect, thanks to the elemi notes. On the other hand, on men skins, the result tends to be different, with an output rich in pepper, a slightly floral evolution and a base of dry aspect and with nuances of cinnamon, a result of the vanilla accord of Heliotrope in conjunction with the patchouli, which can result in a bitter, chocolate or dry accord.

Within what I have already met until today, I would say that this perfume makes an ideal pair with Jaipur (Boucheron) and is very suitable for the colder days of autumn, that anticipate the arrival of winter.

lotus and jasmine 03/26/15 14:46

Do you ever get tired of scents that smell the same? Si Lolita doesn't. The notes in the pyramid above say pink pepper, but I do not detect the rosey scent of pink...instead SL opens with a puckishly intense black pepper accord. Charmingly abrasive, refreshing, odd.

SL is confounding at first. Why would anyone want to smell like black pepper? But...you keep sniffing yourself. Over time, the pepper remains, but drifts of sweet pea, heliotrope, and juicy mandarin catch your attention...

Where are they coming from? You sniff your wrist, and it's still crisp, dark pepper. But that sweetness lingers around you, behind you, where ever you least expect it. Si Lolita sneaks up on the wearer. You'll fall in love with her, after you get to know her. Cinnamon, is not listed, but can be found, anise, clove, and fenugreek as well. Surprisingly bright, given the potential darkness of the accords...but that's the point,right?

But on first acquaintance? She's really not what you expect. Particularly not from a brand known for sweet scents. And why would ANYONE create a perfume that smells like black pepper?

Think Audrey Hepburn. Think flying monkeys. Think of the most gloriously unexpected sights you have ever encountered. An elegance comprised entirely of parts that should not harmonize.

Si Lolita is the Pablo Picasso of perfume, the cubist blue, the scent that is too simple to be true. The unexpected, but much anticipated. the Cirque du Soleil of perfume.

Addictive.
Superlative.
Intoxicating.
Invigorating.
Almost too good to be true.

It's amazing how much one perfume can differ when worn by various people...From other reviews, I expected this to be brasher than it is---much spicier, since that was a constant refrain, and with more aggressive sillage. What I get is a delicate perfume, something ethereal and even sheer, if that may be said of a scent. It reminds me of nothing so much as organza fabric, sheer, subtly iridescent, and quintessentially feminine.

The pink pepper is definitely there, but not at all loudly so. For me, once the initial floral notes dry down, the main thing I smell is the elemi---which is really very nice; a bit of citrus, very light; a bit of pepper, and a lingering floral note, presumably sweet pea. The sweetness of it reminds me of marzipan. It's delicious, not sweet in a nauseating way. When my skin is warmer, the citrus seems to brighten and another note appears that I just can't pin down, almost a wood scent.

Maugli's review resonated with me, both as to the overall experience of a drop-off 10 minutes post-spray followed by a notable change in the scent, and as to the Lutens reference. I also suspect that this will grow on me as I use it. It seems simple, but it's not. Overall I found this a mysterious little perfume and I like mystery...

The spiciness of Si Lolita is no joke. And this comes from someone who loves big spicy bombs like Kenzo Jungle l'Éléphant and enjoys pink pepper heavy scents like Angel EdT (the comet one) or Twilly Eau Poivrée. Si Lolita is floral, sweet, very feminine ; but it's also sharp, raw, unapologetic, it has a big personality. Pink pepper and elemi smell like essential oils, and there seems to be a good dose of cloves here too. Unfortunately, this reminded me of a personal experience : the smell of my dentist's practice. It was all here : the waiting room, the camphorated and sharp disinfectants, and even the rubbery gloves. The lovely sweet floral notes could not tame the medicinal smell. And I have nothing against medicinal scents in general, but when it comes to something reminding me of the dentist, I really can't. Obviously scent perception and skin chemistry are a very personal thing, and Si Lolita certainly doesn't smell like the dentist to most, or it wouldn't have sold well otherwise. I can easily imagine to some people, this strong spicy accord is quite addictive. Unfortunately, it really doesn't work on me. Not a safe blind buy, but I strongly recommend to anyone who likes pink pepper to get a sample of Si Lolita, as it's truly unique.
